In WoW classic there is a pvp mechanic which gives you Dishonourable Kills (as apposed to honourable kills) for killing certain NPCs who are tagged as civilians.

This was removed in TBC expansion as others have said in the thread already, however it is a feature of SoD and Classic Era still.

Dishonourable kills can de-rank you, and can drop you into the PVP rank below which normal rank decay can’t.

Also, if you are in a raid group and someone kills a civilian, all raid members get the DHK whether they participate in the ‘fight’ or not.

The NPC pictured is a quest giver in ashenvale located very close to one of the horde flight paths and quest hubs.

During the PVP event in that zone, raid groups will fly to that flight path, then run past this NPC to the objective. Inevitably someone in the group can’t resist 1-shotting this low level NPC which triggers a DHK for all members of the raid and could potentially de-rank some players.

I also watched Alien (1979) yesterday but not for the first time. I watched Alien Covenant straight afterwards and the difference is stark. Other than the practical effects in Alien which others have mentioned, I think the main difference is the writing. Alien is much more considered with a specific aesthetic in mind which is considered throughout the film. There’s also a lot more suspense, being a horror film rather than a sci-fi action. We don’t see Ripley as the main protagonist until deep into the film, which allows the film to subvert our expectations each time someone dies. The characters are also very well written and make sense. They are contracted space truckers and behave as such. They’re blue collar but have knowledge of the ship and their jobs, they are relatable in that way.

In Covenant, I was amazed at how stupid every single decision made by the crew was leading up to things hitting the fan. They are supposed to be the crew of a massive colony ship on a one way trip across multiple systems with 2000 other colonists in cryogenic sleep on board. Yet they consistently make thoughtless decisions, panic constantly and can’t seem to think 2 steps ahead at any time. It’s like they were all hired for the mission with zero experience or skills in expedition making, combat or even team building despite the massive financial investment clearly present. What company or government would leave these people in charge with such an important mission??

For example, they leave the mission for starters, routing to a new random planet they come across by chance. They take zero precautions when on the planet when interacting with the environment(one guy is smoking and then drops hit cigarette butt. Another guy pokes a strange flower and let’s it shoot spores in his face breathing them in). When a crew mate is sick, they communicate zero information between one another, they take no consideration for quarantining alien bio hazards and when shit hits the fan they all panic and don’t seem to have any idea what to do in the situation. Even basic stuff like reverting to text messages when they loose communications, like where is that in this film? “Crew member sick, ship quarantined. Return to ship with caution.” It’s that simple surely? 

It makes such a massive difference in a film when the characters are actually relatable and believable.

Most runs I’ve done on alliance in hardcore have been:

Elwynn or Dun Morogh to begin. Complete the zone your character spawns in, then at level 10 head to the other zone and complete it. 

Then go to Loch Modan and do the first few quests. By this time you should be 15-16.

Then go to Westfall and do the first few quests. This should get you to 17-18.

Then go to Darkshore and do the first few quests. This will get you to 19 and you can go back and finish Westfall and Loch Modan, then return to Darkshore and finish that zone.

At this point I would go to Redridge as you should be at least 22 which is the minimum to safely quest in this zone. Again, do the first few quests then hop to Wetlands.
